sentences.en: There are political fireworks in Britain this morning over a surprise move today by British
sentences.zh: 今天早上，英国首相鲍里斯·约翰逊采取了暂停议会的突发举措，这在英国引发了政治风暴。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Boris Johnson to suspend Parliament.
sentences.zh: 首相鲍里斯·约翰逊今天采取了暂停议会的突发举措，引发了英国政治上的轩然大波。

sentences.en: Now, here's what it will do.

sentences.en: Parliament was supposed to sit again on Monday for a number of weeks, but instead this will suspend Parliament the week of September 10th, and it won't resume until October 14th.
sentences.zh: 议会本应在周一恢复开会数周，但取而代之的是，这将从9月10日这一周开始暂停议会，直到10月14日才会复会。

sentences.en: So, in our last episode about Brexit, we spoke to our colleague, Katrin Benhold, just after
sentences.zh: 所以在我们上一期关于脱欧的节目中，我们采访了我们的同事卡特琳·本霍尔德，当时

sentences.en: Boris Johnson had suspended Parliament and basically cut them out of the decision-making process about how Brexit would move forward.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊刚刚暂停了议会，基本上将他们排除了关于脱欧如何推进的决策过程之外。

sentences.en: And Katrin talked about how that had set up this question about what version of democracy would prevail in Britain.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳谈到，这引发了一个问题，即英国究竟会确立哪种版本的民主。

sentences.en: Should it be the version that prioritizes the popular will of the British people who voted for Brexit with or without a deal with the EU, which is what Boris Johnson wants?
sentences.zh: 是应该优先考虑英国人民的民意，即无论是否与欧盟达成协议都投票支持脱欧的民意——这也是鲍里斯·约翰逊想要的？

sentences.en: Or should the version of democracy be allowing Parliament, the people's representatives, to play a major role in what leaving the EU looks like?
sentences.zh: 还是应该选择让议会（即人民的代表）在英国脱欧的具体形式中发挥主要作用的民主版本？

sentences.en: So, how has this all unfolded in the days since Boris Johnson made that move?
sentences.zh: 那么，自从鲍里斯·约翰逊采取这一举动以来，这一切都是如何发展的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think the answer is that it unfolded resoundingly in favor of Parliament.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想答案是，事态的发展完全对议会有利。

sentences.en: As Parliament reconvened on Tuesday, because remember, Boris Johnson's suspension of Parliament doesn't kick in for another week or so.
sentences.zh: 随着议会在周二复会，因为记住，鲍里斯·约翰逊暂停议会的决定还要过一周左右才会生效。

sentences.en: He wouldn't dare behave like that in front of...
sentences.zh: 他绝对不敢在...

sentences.en: With MPs going on TV, on the radio.
sentences.zh: 议员们纷纷上电视、上广播。

sentences.en: There used to be this phrase, the One Nation Tory.

sentences.en: And this leader, I don't recognize this.

sentences.en: It's a Brexit party.

sentences.en: Rebadge.

sentences.en: Look.
sentences.zh: 看。

sentences.en: Complaining about Boris Johnson having committed a constitutional outrage.
sentences.zh: 抱怨鲍里斯·约翰逊犯下了违宪的暴行。

sentences.en: It is a constitutional outrage.
sentences.zh: 这确实是违宪的暴行。

sentences.en: This is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: He needs to be held to account by Parliament, not by shutting down Parliament.
sentences.zh: 他需要接受议会的问责，而不是通过关停议会来逃避。

sentences.en: And all of this emotion climaxed...
sentences.zh: 所有这些情绪在最后达到了高潮……

sentences.en: And of course, I think one of the most remarkable things that took place during the statement was to see the member for Bracknell cross the floor.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为声明期间发生的最引人注目的事情之一，就是看到布拉克内尔的议员倒戈。

sentences.en: Prime Minister, you have lost your majority.
sentences.zh: 首相先生，你已经失去了多数席位。

sentences.en: With a member of Boris Johnson's own Conservative Party crossing the aisle in front of the Prime
sentences.zh: 随着鲍里斯·约翰逊自己保守党的一名议员在首相面前跨过议会走廊，

sentences.en: Minister to sit with members of the Liberal Democratic Party, an act which deprived Johnson, in one stroke of his majority in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 加入自由民主党议员的阵营，这一举动一举剥夺了约翰逊在议会中的多数优势。

sentences.en: He isn't winning friends in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他在欧洲没有赢得朋友。

sentences.en: He's losing friends at home.
sentences.zh: 他在国内正在失去朋友。

sentences.en: This is a government with no mandate, no morals, and as of today, no majority.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有授权、没有道德、而且从今天起没有多数席位的政府。

sentences.en: So after this very stormy start, the next thing that happens is...
sentences.zh: 所以在经历了这个暴风雨般的开局之后，接下来发生的事情是……

sentences.en: Tonight the United Kingdom has been plunged into even deeper political chaos.
sentences.zh: 今晚，英国陷入了更深重的政治混乱。

sentences.en: The opposition, joined by 21 members of the Conservative Party, vote in favour of advancing this legislation,
sentences.zh: 反对派与保守党的21名议员联手，投票赞成推进这项立法，

sentences.en: that would effectively say to Boris Johnson, you can't go to Brussels and pull Britain out of the European Union unless you make a deal with the European Union firSt.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是在对鲍里斯·约翰逊说，除非你先与欧盟达成协议，否则你不能去布鲁塞尔把英国拉出欧盟。

sentences.en: The majority of British lawmakers, including some members of Prime Minister Boris Johnson's own party,
sentences.zh: 英国大多数议员，包括首相鲍里斯·约翰逊自己党内的一些成员，

sentences.en: voted to stop Johnson's plan to leave the European Union without a withdrawal agreement.
sentences.zh: 投票反对约翰逊在没有达成脱欧协议的情况下离开欧盟的计划。

sentences.en: Not a good start, Boris.
sentences.zh: 开局不利啊，鲍里斯。

sentences.en: The eyes to the right, 328.
sentences.zh: 赞成票在右侧，328票。

sentences.en: The nose to the left, 301.
sentences.zh: 反对票在左侧，301票。

sentences.en: So the eyes have it.
sentences.zh: 因此，赞成票获胜。

sentences.en: The eyes have it.
sentences.zh: 赞成票获胜。

sentences.en: Unlock.
sentences.zh: 解锁。

sentences.en: So that's the first major defeat he suffers in his term as Prime Minister, and it's a big one.
sentences.zh: 这是他担任首相以来遭遇的第一次重大失败，而且是一次惨败。

sentences.en: There is no consent in this House to leave the European Union without a deal.
sentences.zh: 本议会绝不同意在无协议的情况下离开欧盟。

sentences.en: There is no majority for no deal in the country.
sentences.zh: 全国上下对于无协议脱欧也没有多数共识。

sentences.en: Because it goes straight to the heart of what Boris Johnson said he would do as Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 因为这直接触及了鲍里斯·约翰逊承诺担任首相时要做的事情的核心。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And that is to withdraw on October 31st, deal or no deal, regardless of this situation.
sentences.zh: 那就是在10月31日退出，无论有无协议，也不管当前的局势如何。

sentences.en: So when that one conservative lawmaker theatrically flipped on the floor of Parliament, it turned out that was a signal of a bigger, growing uprising within Boris Johnson's party
sentences.zh: 因此，当那位保守党议员在议会大厅戏剧性地倒戈时，事实证明，这是鲍里斯·约翰逊党内一场更大、不断壮大的起义的信号，

sentences.en: over this approach he was taking to Brexit to try to cut Parliament out and just kind of crash this thing through.
sentences.zh: 起因是他采取这种试图将议会排除在外、强行推进脱欧的方针。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's really very unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 这真的是史无前例的。

sentences.en: I mean, the Conservative Party, British parties in general, have iron discipline.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，保守党，英国的政党普遍有着铁的纪律。

sentences.en: So to see 21 lawmakers peel off and vote against the Prime Minister and the government is really a wholly unprecedented development in British politics.
sentences.zh: 因此，看到21名议员脱离并投票反对首相和政府，在英国政治中确实是一个完全前所未有的发展。

sentences.en: So from the very first session of Parliament, the British people understood that what they were witnessing was something entirely new in their modern political history.
sentences.zh: 因此，从议会的第一次会议开始，英国人民就明白，他们所见证的是其现代政治史上的全新事物。

sentences.en: And what exactly is underlying these defections and rejection of Boris Johnson's plan?
sentences.zh: 这些反叛和拒绝鲍里斯·约翰逊计划的背后到底是什么原因？

sentences.en: I mean, why is this so unwanted that even members of his own party are rising up against him?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么这个计划如此不受欢迎，以至于连他自己党内的成员都起来反对他？

sentences.en: Well, the basic fear is that if Britain withdraws from the European Union with no agreement in place, overnight, it will cause a multitude of major probleMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最基本的恐惧是，如果英国在没有达成任何协议的情况下退出欧盟，一夜之间就会引发一大堆重大问题。

sentences.en: You could imagine trucks that transport food and medicine from Europe into Britain being stuck at the border in Calais in France.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，从欧洲运输食品和药品到英国的卡车会被困在法国加来边境。

sentences.en: You could imagine chaos at the airports as people who are used to traveling back and forth without passports suddenly face the prospect of having to show identification.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象机场的混乱，那些习惯了不带护照来回旅行的人突然面临必须出示身份证明的前景。

sentences.en: You risk, in short, havoc.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，你面临着浩劫的风险。

sentences.en: Havoc that could really hurt the economy, but could also further polarize the debate over Brexit.
sentences.zh: 这场浩劫不仅会严重损害经济，还会进一步加剧关于脱欧的争论。

sentences.en: So I think that even within Boris Johnson's party, which, remember, is a party that wholeheartedly supports the goal of pulling out of Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，甚至在鲍里斯·约翰逊的党内——请记住，这是一个全心全意支持脱欧目标的政党——

sentences.en: The idea of pulling out in this disorderly, abrupt way just scared a lot of the members of Johnson's own party.
sentences.zh: 这种混乱、突然的退欧想法也让约翰逊自己党内的许多成员感到害怕。

sentences.en: And that fear is what motivated this rebellion.
sentences.zh: 正是这种恐惧激发了这场叛乱。

sentences.en: But to these 21 rebels, he's setting Britain on a course that they feel ultimately will be economically and politically destructive.
sentences.zh: 但对于这21名叛乱分子来说，他正在把英国带上一条他们认为最终会在经济和政治上带来破坏的道路。

sentences.en: So they view their role as saying, hey, wait a minute, we want to deliver Brexit, but we want to do it in a responsible way.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们认为自己的角色是：嘿，等等，我们想要实现脱欧，但我们要以负责任的方式去做。

sentences.en: And this is not the responsible way to do it.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是负责任的做法。

sentences.en: So how did the prime minister respond to this rebellion, to this move in parliament?
sentences.zh: 那么首相是如何回应这场叛乱、回应议会中的这一举动的呢？

sentences.en: Boris Johnson does two things.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊做了两件事。

sentences.en: The ruling conservatives are in turmoil.
sentences.zh: 执政的保守党陷入了一片混乱。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson has kicked out 21 members of his own party after they voted against him to seize control of the parliamentary agenda.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊将自己党内的21名议员开除出党，此前他们投票反对他，以夺取对议会议程的控制权。

sentences.en: The first thing he does is he carries out what you almost have to call a Stalinist purge of these rebels.
sentences.zh: 他做的第一件事，就是对这些叛乱分子进行了一场几乎可以说是斯大林式的清洗。

sentences.en: He kicks them out of the party.
sentences.zh: 他把他们踢出了党。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I would have to say Boris Johnson really had the worst week.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说鲍里斯·约翰逊真的度过了最糟糕的一周。

sentences.en: I mean, here he is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他才刚上任。

sentences.en: He's new.
sentences.zh: 他是新人。

sentences.en: He lost every one of his first votes in parliament, which is unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 他在议会的前几次投票中全部失利，这真是史无前例。

sentences.en: He purged 21 people in his own party because they didn't support him.
sentences.zh: 他清洗了党内的21名异己，因为他们不支持他。

sentences.en: I mean, and I think it's kind of stunning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这简直太惊人了。

sentences.en: And it leads to this extraordinary tableau of these conservative MPs, some of whom have served for decades, some of whom are elders of the party,
sentences.zh: 这呈现出一幅非同寻常的画面：那些保守党议员们，其中有些人服务了几十年，有些是党内的元老，

sentences.en: giving these emotional farewell speeches in the House of Commons.
sentences.zh: 在下议院发表了这些充满情感的告别演讲。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Speaking very emotionally about all the years he spent in parliament.
sentences.zh: 饱含深情地谈论他在议会度过的所有岁月。

sentences.en: You have titans of British politics like Kenneth Clark, who's known as the father of the House, a former chancellor of the Exchequer,
sentences.zh: 英国政治界的中流砥柱，比如肯尼斯·克拉克（Kenneth Clark），被称为下议院之父、前财政大臣，

sentences.en: a man who might well have been prime minister himself.
sentences.zh: 一个本有可能自己当上首相的人。

sentences.en: Do you recognize your party tonight?
sentences.zh: 今晚你还认得你的党吗？

sentences.en: No, it's been taken over by a rather knockabout sort of character who's got this bizarre crash it through philosophy in charge.
sentences.zh: 不，它被一个相当粗鲁无礼的角色接管了，他带着这种离奇的硬闯哲学掌权。

sentences.en: Talking about a political situation and a party that they no longer recognized.
sentences.zh: 谈论一个他们再也认不出来的政治局势和一个政党。

sentences.en: A cabinet which is the most right-wing cabinet any conservative party's ever produced.
sentences.zh: 这是一个保守党历史上最右翼的内阁。

sentences.en: But the prime minister comes and talks total rubbish to us.
sentences.zh: 但首相来到我们面前，对我们大放厥词。

sentences.en: And so it was this really dramatic moment where you saw pillars of the British political establishment just suddenly knock down in the most brutal fashion.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常戏剧性的时刻，你看到英国政治建制派的顶梁柱以最残酷的方式突然被击倒。

sentences.en: Mark, why would the prime minister do this to members of his own party, basically inflict this kind of damage to his own members at a time when he, I have to imagine,
sentences.zh: 马克，首相为什么要对自己的党员这样做，基本上是在他自己想象中

sentences.en: needs them more than ever?
sentences.zh: 比以往任何时候都更需要他们的时候，给自己的成员造成这种伤害？

sentences.en: Shouldn't he be, you know, cozying up to them?
sentences.zh: 难道他不应该，你知道的，去讨好他们吗？

sentences.en: You would think so.
sentences.zh: 你本会这么想的。

sentences.en: But above all, what Boris Johnson wants to do is send a message of ideological purity to his pro-Brexit voters.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，鲍里斯·约翰逊（Boris Johnson）想要向他支持脱欧的选民发出一个纯正意识形态的信号。

sentences.en: He wants to tell those voters that I'm going to rid the party of anyone that will stand in the way of getting Britain out of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 他想告诉这些选民，我要将党内任何阻碍英国脱离欧盟的人清除出去。

sentences.en: So this was less about settling scores with MPs, many of whom he's known well for years served with.
sentences.zh: 所以这与其说是在跟议员们算账——其中许多人他认识多年、共事多年，

sentences.en: It's really more about sending this emphatic message to the hardcore pro-Brexit constituency that increasingly drives the conservative party and saying,
sentences.zh: 不如说是在向日益掌控保守党的强硬脱欧派选民发出这个强烈的信号，并表示，

sentences.en: we are not going to let anything slow us down, including these internal obstacles.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会让任何事情放慢我们的脚步，包括这些内部障碍。

sentences.en: So this is very much in keeping with the prime minister's message that this is now his party, the conservative party, the party of the people of the Brexiteers.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合首相传递的信息：现在这是他的党，保守党，人民的党，脱欧派的党。

sentences.en: And if you're not with me and if you're not with them, then who needs you?
sentences.zh: 如果你不跟我在一起，如果你不和他们站在一起，那么谁还需要你？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It basically is unambiguous.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是毋庸置疑的。

sentences.en: It's emphatic.
sentences.zh: 这是斩钉截铁的。

sentences.en: He does not leave himself open to any charge of being soft on Brexit, ready to do a deal, ready to compromise.
sentences.zh: 他没有给自己留下任何被指责对脱欧态度软弱、准备达成协议、准备妥协的借口。

sentences.en: So you said that there were two things he did.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才说他做了两件事。

sentences.en: What was the second?
sentences.zh: 第二件是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the second thing he did is he called for a snap election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他做的第二件事是呼吁举行突击大选。

sentences.en: The country must now decide whether the leader of the opposition or I go to those negotiations in Brussels on the 17th of October to sort this out.
sentences.zh: 现在国家必须决定，是反对党领袖还是我，在10月17日前往布鲁塞尔的谈判中解决这个问题。

sentences.en: He said, in effect, I think the only way to resolve this impasse is to go to the voters.
sentences.zh: 他实际上说，我认为解决这种僵局的唯一方法就是诉诸选民。

sentences.en: If they want what I've offered, which is a swift exit from Europe, then they will give me a mandate to go to Brussels and do that.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想要我提供的方案，也就是迅速退出欧洲，那么他们会给我授权去布鲁塞尔完成这件事。

sentences.en: If they don't want that, I'll be defeated and someone else can go to Brussels.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不想要这个，我就会被击败，别人可以去布鲁塞尔。

sentences.en: And Mark, the prime minister can do that.
sentences.zh: 马克，首相确实可以这么做。

sentences.en: He can call for an election whenever it's politically convenient for him and try to change the composition of the government that might stand in his way.
sentences.zh: 只要对他的政治有利，他随时可以呼吁大选，并试图改变可能阻碍他的政府的组成。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's one of the prerogatives of the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是首相的特权之一。

sentences.en: And in Boris Johnson's case, he's viewing this in a couple of ways.
sentences.zh: 就鲍里斯·约翰逊而言，他从几个方面来看待这个问题。

sentences.en: One, if he wins, he gets a popular mandate to go to Brussels and drive a hard bargain with the European Commission and presumably emerge with a better deal for Britain.
sentences.zh: 第一，如果他赢了，他将获得民意授权去布鲁塞尔，与欧盟委员会进行艰难的谈判，并大概能为英国争取到一个更好的协议。

sentences.en: On a more practical level, if he wins,
sentences.zh: 从更实际的层面来看，如果他赢了，

sentences.en: there'll be more conservative party members sitting in parliament and some of the bad arithmetic he's been facing on votes related to Brexit become much easier for him.
sentences.zh: 议会中将会有更多保守党议员，他在脱欧相关投票中一直面临的不利算术将变得容易得多。

sentences.en: But there is a wrinkle to all this, which is that although he has the right to call an election, he needs a two thirds vote in parliament to get an election schedule.
sentences.zh: 但这一切有一个转折，那就是尽管他有权呼吁大选，但他需要在议会中获得三分之二的投票才能安排大选日程。

sentences.en: So he has the power to call it, but he still needs to bring a majority of the existing parliament behind him in order to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 所以他有权力呼吁选举，但他仍然需要争取现有议会多数的支持才能实现这一点。

sentences.en: So do these tactics work for Boris Johnson, expelling disloyal conservatives and threatening an election that could give him a mandate and weaken the opposition?
sentences.zh: 那么这些策略对鲍里斯·约翰逊管用吗？驱逐不忠的保守派，并威胁举行可能赋予他授权并削弱反对党的大选？

sentences.en: The short answer is no, because the very next day, everything goes against him.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是不会，因为就在第二天，一切都对A他不利。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权。

sentences.en: So, Mark, Boris Johnson calls for a special election, but it turns out he needs a two-thirds vote from parliament to make that happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，马克，鲍里斯·约翰逊呼吁举行特别大选，但结果证明他需要议会三分之二的投票才能实现这一点。

sentences.en: So what actually happens?
sentences.zh: 那么实际上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Opposition leaders have roundly rejected his call for a general election next month.
sentences.zh: 反对党领袖已经断然拒绝了他关于下个月举行大选的呼吁。

sentences.en: He doesn't get his two-thirds majority for an election.
sentences.zh: 他没有获得举行选举所需的三分之二多数票。

sentences.en: Mr. Johnson declared he had never known an opposition in the history of democracy that's refused to have an election.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊先生宣称，他从未在民主历史上见过哪个反对派拒绝举行大选。

sentences.en: So in effect, he's stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，他被卡住了。

sentences.en: He's boxed in on his big goal of pulling Britain out of the EU, and he's not able to move ahead with the election.
sentences.zh: 他在把英国拉出欧盟这一宏伟目标上陷入了困境，而且无法推进大选。

sentences.en: The thing he was hoping would break the logjam would give him the mandate.
sentences.zh: 他原本希望这件事能打破僵局，给他带来授权。

sentences.en: So basically, this all backfires.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这一切适得其反。

sentences.en: It all backfires.
sentences.zh: 这一切都适得其反。

sentences.en: He loses more votes than any incoming prime minister in recent British history, and he finds himself in far worse shape than he was before all this started.
sentences.zh: 他失去的票数比近代英国历史上的任何一位新任首相都要多，他发现自己的处境比这一切开始之前要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that leaves the Brexit situation where exactly?
sentences.zh: 那这到底让脱欧局势处于什么境地？

sentences.en: Well, it leaves, frankly, everything in a state of paralysis and confusion.
sentences.zh: 嗯，坦白说，这让一切都陷入了瘫痪和混乱的状态。

sentences.en: By the end of the week in London, one of the questions on people's minds were, would Boris Johnson simply have to resign?
sentences.zh: 到了伦敦本周末，人们心中的疑问之一就是：鲍里斯·约翰逊难道不得不直接辞职吗？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, if you take the prime minister at his word.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你相信首相的话。

sentences.en: Can you make a promise today to the British public that you will not go back to Brussels and ask for another delay to Brexit?
sentences.zh: 你今天能否向英国公众做出承诺，你不会再回到布鲁塞尔要求推迟脱欧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And would you rather...
sentences.zh: 你宁愿……

sentences.en: I'd rather be dead in a ditch.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿死在沟里。

sentences.en: I hate banging on about Brexit.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌喋喋不休地谈论脱欧。

sentences.en: He has said he would rather die in a ditch than have to go to Brussels and ask for an extension of Britain's departure.
sentences.zh: 他曾说过，他宁愿死在沟里，也不愿去布鲁塞尔要求延长英国的退欧期限。

sentences.en: Yet, as things stand today, that's exactly what Boris Johnson will have to do.
sentences.zh: 然而，就目前的情况来看，这正是鲍里斯·约翰逊将不得不做的事情。

sentences.en: And if all of this were not enough this week of back-to-back defeats, Boris Johnson had to endure the indignity of his own brother, Joe Johnson,
sentences.zh: 如果这连续几天的失败还不够的话，鲍里斯·约翰逊还不得不忍受他自己的亲弟弟乔·约翰逊（Joe Johnson）带来的耻辱，

sentences.en: who is also a member of parliament and a minister in the government,
sentences.zh: 他也是一名国会议员兼政府大臣，

sentences.en: announcing that he, too, was going to resign because, as he put it, he was torn between family loyalty and the national intereSt.
sentences.zh: 宣布他也要辞职，因为正如他所说，他在家族忠诚和国家利益之间感到左右为难。

sentences.en: Tell us when you're planning to resign.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你打算什么时候辞职。

sentences.en: I haven't had any further comments to say, other than it's been an honor to be MP for all-point-time and a minister under three governments.
sentences.zh: 除了表示很荣幸能担任全体议员以及在三届政府下担任大臣之外，我没有其他进一步的评论要说。

sentences.en: But it's time to move on, and I've got to get to work.
sentences.zh: 但现在是向前看的时候了，我得去工作了。

sentences.en: Do you think your brother's writing the party?
sentences.zh: 你认为你弟弟在写信给这个党吗？

sentences.en: Sorry, I beg your pardon.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，请再说一遍。

sentences.en: See you, folks.
sentences.zh: 再见，伙计们。

sentences.en: This is a very tight-knit family.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关系非常紧密的家庭。

sentences.en: So the fact that Joe Johnson felt obliged to take this step really says something about the depth of his concern about a no-deal Brexit,
sentences.zh: 因此，乔·约翰逊觉得有必要采取这一步骤，这确实说明了他对无协议脱欧的担忧程度，

sentences.en: about the course that his brother Boris Johnson has the country going on.
sentences.zh: 以及对他哥哥鲍里斯·约翰逊正带领国家走向的道路的担忧。

sentences.en: So just to be clear, those people opposed to Johnson right now in parliament, they are insisting on going back to the European Union to negotiate some kind of an exit.
sentences.zh: 所以为了明确起见，目前在议会中反对约翰逊的那些人，他们坚持要回到欧盟去谈判某种形式的退欧。

sentences.en: And so if Johnson is unwilling to do that, he might be out of office.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果约翰逊不愿这样做，他可能会下台。

sentences.en: But I guess the question is, is the EU willing to actually enter these kinds of negotiations?
sentences.zh: 但我想问题是，欧盟真的愿意进行这种谈判吗？

sentences.en: Aren't they pretty fed up with Britain at this point?
sentences.zh: 他们现在对英国不是很厌烦了吗？

sentences.en: The EU is completely fed up with Britain at this point.
sentences.zh: 欧盟现在对英国完全厌烦了。

sentences.en: They believe that they had months of good-faith negotiations with Boris Johnson's predecessor, Theresa May.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他们与鲍里斯·约翰逊的前任特雷莎·梅（Theresa May）进行了几个月的诚意谈判。

sentences.en: They offered her an agreement.
sentences.zh: 他们向她提供了一项协议。

sentences.en: She brought that agreement back to parliament.
sentences.zh: 她把那个协议带回了议会。

sentences.en: It was overwhelmingly defeated, not once, but several times.
sentences.zh: 它被压倒性地否决了，不是一次，而是好几次。

sentences.en: And there's absolutely no indication from European officials that Boris Johnson is going to get a better or different outcome than Theresa May did.
sentences.zh: 而且没有任何迹象表明欧洲官员认为鲍里斯·约翰逊会比特雷莎·梅取得更好或不同的结果。

sentences.en: And whether or not he holds an election is being largely dismissed in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他在欧洲是否举行大选基本被忽视了。

sentences.en: Their view is, we have given Britain the best deal it's going to get.
sentences.zh: 他们的观点是，我们已经给了英国最好的协议。

sentences.en: And if Britain doesn't want that deal, it's time for them to simply leave.
sentences.zh: 如果英国不想要这个协议，那他们就该直接离开。

sentences.en: What do you make of this remarkable sequence of events, your first full week as London Bureau Chief?
sentences.zh: 作为伦敦分社社长的第一个完整周，你对这一连串非凡的事件有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, there's a couple of ways to look at it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几种看待它的方式。

sentences.en: One is that this is just a situation of overwhelming chaos, confusion, paralysis, finger pointing.
sentences.zh: 一种是，这只是一种充满混乱、困惑、瘫痪、互相指责的局面。

sentences.en: So on one level, it looks like dysfunction, you know, on a grand scale.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，它看起来像是大规模的失调。

sentences.en: But if you dig beyond that, if you sort of look a little closer,
sentences.zh: 但如果你深入挖掘，如果你仔细观察一下，

sentences.en: what you see is that this was really a week in which the checks and balances in the British political system really worked.
sentences.zh: 你会发现这确实是一个英国政治体制中的制衡机制真正发挥作用的一周。

sentences.en: You have the prime minister coming in with this hardline, even reckless approach to Brexit, embodied in his decision to suspend debate in parliament,
sentences.zh: 你有首相带着这种强硬甚至鲁莽的脱欧方式上台，体现在他决定暂停议会辩论，

sentences.en: to sort of circumvent the normal functioning of parliament by sending the MPs home.
sentences.zh: 通过遣散议员来变相规避议会的正常运转。

sentences.en: And then you've got this coalition of members of his own party and the opposition coming together to put a break on the prime minister,
sentences.zh: 然后你又有他自己党内的成员和反对派组成的联盟联合起来，对首相踩刹车，

sentences.en: to head off some of these most extreme outcomes.
sentences.zh: 以阻止一些最极端的结果。

sentences.en: And that's kind of what makes British democracy so unique, that there is this set of conventions, of folkways that impose a level of moderation on these proceedings.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国民主如此独特的原因，存在着这样一套惯例和习俗，对这些程序施加了一定程度的温和控制。

sentences.en: And we really did see a victory for that in parliament, a victory that was not at all clear when the House of Commons convened at the beginning of the week.
sentences.zh: 我们在议会中确实看到了这一点的胜利，而当下议院在周初开会时，这种胜利还完全不明朗。

sentences.en: So Mark, you're saying that even though this all looked especially chaotic, that actually what we just saw was democratic institutions holding, functioning, and succeeding.
sentences.zh: 所以马克，你的意思是，尽管这一切看起来人格外混乱，但实际上我们刚刚看到的是民主机构在坚守、运转并取得成功。

sentences.en: But of course, the other way of looking at this, and the way Boris Johnson, I assume, looks at it, is that the will of the people has just been subverted,
sentences.zh: 但当然，另一种看待方式，也是我猜想鲍里斯·约翰逊看待它的方式，是民意刚刚被颠覆了，

sentences.en: that they want Brexit with or without a deal, and that parliament, what you just described as the kind of assertive functioning of democracy in Britain, just stood in their way.
sentences.zh: 他们想要有协议或无协议的脱欧，而议会——你刚才形容为英国民主自信运转的产物——正好挡了他们的路。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Boris Johnson's argument will be, I want to go to the people, to put this to the people.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊的论点将是，我要诉诸人民，将这一点交由人民决定。

sentences.en: And these MPs, Britain's political elite, is standing in the way of popular sentiment.
sentences.zh: 而这些议员，英国的政治精英，正挡在民意的对立面。

sentences.en: And that will be the core of the message that he brings to the British public as he attempts to turn this situation around.
sentences.zh: 这将成为他试图扭转这种局面时带给英国公众的核心信息。

sentences.en: And how are you feeling that the British system is holding up compared to the American system that you know so well?
sentences.zh: 与你非常熟悉的美国体制相比，你觉得英国体制的支撑情况如何？

sentences.en: If we put these two democracies side by side, how does it stack up?
sentences.zh: 如果我们把这两个民主国家放在一起比较，情况如何？

sentences.en: Well, one thing that is very striking to me in covering this rebellion in the Conservative Party is to compare it to the Republican Party in the United States.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在报道保守党内部这场叛乱时，令我非常震撼的一点是将其与美国的共和党进行比较。

sentences.en: And there, of course, you see barely a handful of Republicans who have stood up to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 在那里，当然，你几乎看不到有几个共和党人站出来反对特朗普总统。

sentences.en: This is a Republican Party that is 100% under his control.
sentences.zh: 这是一个百分之百在他控制之下的共和党。

sentences.en: He has engineered a total takeover of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 他策划了对共和党的大权独揽。

sentences.en: I think Boris Johnson tried in the past two weeks to do the same thing over here.
sentences.zh: 我认为鲍里斯·约翰逊在过去两周里也试图在这里做到这一点。

sentences.en: I think this rebellion shows that the party wasn't going to stand for it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这场叛乱表明该党不会容忍这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's also fair to say that Boris Johnson's having a tougher time in his populist crusade than Donald Trump is in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，鲍里斯·约翰逊在他的民粹主义十字军东征中比唐纳德·特朗普在美国过得更艰难。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: After we spoke with Mark, another member of Boris Johnson's Conservative Party resigned in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 在我们与马克交谈后，鲍里斯·约翰逊保守党的另一名成员愤而辞职以示抗议。

sentences.en: This time, a top minister in his government, Amber Rudd, who said she could not sit by and watch what she called Johnson's, quote, assault on decency and democracy.
sentences.zh: 这一次是他政府中的高级大臣安伯·拉德（Amber Rudd），她表示她无法坐视不管并看着她所谓的约翰逊对体面和民主的“攻击”。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: The Trump administration said it was calling off, for now, the year-long negotiations between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府表示，在塔利班宣称对喀布尔导致12人死亡（包括一名美国士兵）的汽车炸弹袭击负责后，

sentences.en: and the Taliban to end the war in Afghanistan after the Taliban took credit for a car bombing in Kabul that killed 12 people, including a U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国与塔利班为期一年的旨在结束阿富汗战争的谈判将暂时叫停。

sentences.en: soldier.
sentences.zh: 士兵。

sentences.en: We're going to walk away from a deal if others try to use violence to achieve better ends in a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 如果其他人试图在谈判中使用暴力来达到更好的目的，我们将退出协议。

sentences.en: It's not right.
sentences.zh: 这是不对的。

sentences.en: It's not appropriate.
sentences.zh: 这是不合适的。

sentences.en: It killed an American.
sentences.zh: 它夺去了美国人的生命。

sentences.en: And it made no sense for the Taliban to be rewarded for that kind of bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 塔利班因这种不良行为而受到奖励是没有任何意义的。

sentences.en: The negotiations appeared to be on the verge of a peace deal,
sentences.zh: 谈判似乎正处于达成和平协议的边缘，

sentences.en: so much so that leaders of the Taliban and the Afghan government were on their way to Camp David for a secret meeting with Trump.
sentences.zh: 以至于塔利班和阿富汗政府的领导人正在前往戴维营与特朗普进行秘密会晤的路上。

sentences.en: A meeting Secretary of State Mike Pompeo defended on Sunday in interviews with CNN and NBC.
sentences.zh: 美国国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥（Mike Pompeo）周日在接受美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）和全国广播公司（NBC）采访时为这次会晤进行了辩护。

sentences.en: Did anybody bring up whether it was appropriate to have the Taliban set foot on Camp David?
sentences.zh: 有没有人提出过，让塔利班踏上戴维营是否合适？

sentences.en: Well, there were lots of discussions around that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，围绕这一点有很多讨论。

sentences.en: Camp David has a long history, an important history, and it's also had an important role in complex peace negotiations, sometimes with some pretty bad actors, as you well know,
sentences.zh: 戴维营有着悠久的历史、重要的历史，而且它在复杂的和平谈判中也发挥过重要作用，有时谈判对象还是些相当恶劣的角色，正如你很清楚的那样，

sentences.en: Chuck.
sentences.zh: 查克。

sentences.en: The Taliban had not agreed to stop attacking Americans in advance of a peace deal.
sentences.zh: 塔利班在达成和平协议之前并没有同意停止袭击美国人。

sentences.en: But in a tweet, Trump wrote, quote,
sentences.zh: 但特朗普在一条推文中写道，引述：

sentences.en: If they cannot agree to a ceasefire during these very important peace talks, and would even kill 12 innocent people,
sentences.zh: 如果他们在这些非常重要的和平谈判期间无法同意停火，甚至还要杀害12名无辜平民，

sentences.en: then they probably don't have the power to negotiate a meaningful agreement anyway.
sentences.zh: 那么他们大概也没有能力谈判达成一份有意义的协议。

sentences.en: And the leader of a prestigious lab at MIT has resigned from the university and from the board of the New York Times over revelations that he solicited far greater donations from Jeffrey Epstein than previously known and tried to hide the source of the money.
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院一个知名实验室的负责人已经辞去了大学职务以及《纽约时报》董事会的职务，此前有爆料称，他从杰弗里·爱泼斯坦那里索取了比以往所知更多的捐款，并试图隐瞒资金来源。

sentences.en: The New Yorker magazine reported that the lab's director, Joey Ito,
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》杂志报道称，该实验室的主任伊藤穰一，

sentences.en: instructed staff to conceal Epstein's donations as anonymous to avoid scrutiny of his record as a sex offender who had solicited minors.
sentences.zh: 指示员工将爱泼斯坦的捐款伪装成匿名捐款，以逃避对其作为曾诱拐未成年人的性犯罪者的审查。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时的选举迎来了许多自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的权力之争。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》播客中，由我萨拉·科尼格为您讲述一些人试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在各大播客平台收听。
